stops.note: the staple drink of steppe nomads; the friar William of Rubruck described it at the Mongol court in 1254
Russian doctors prescribed 'kumys cures' on the steppe for tuberculosis; Leo Tolstoy took one in the Samara steppe in 1862
English followed the Russian form, since most Western travellers met the drink in Russian-ruled lands

current_meaning: fermented mare's milk, the traditional drink of Central Asian nomads
